6º de Primaria · Inglés

Reading and writing an email

Ficha para imprimir
123456
1

Pregunta de arranquePiensa 30 segundos antes de seguir

Si escribes a un amigo de Inglaterra, ¿empezarías con «Dear Sir» o con «Hi Tom»? ¿Y cómo te despedirías?

Escribe o di en voz alta tu respuesta. Después .

Con un amigo usamos un email informal: «Hi Tom,» o «Dear Tom,» para empezar y «Love,», «Bye for now,» o «Best wishes,» para terminar. «Dear Sir or Madam» se usa en correos formales, por ejemplo para escribir a una empresa.

2

Aprende14 apartados

Para empezar: Christmas on the beach

From: Mia
To: Pablo
Subject: Christmas on the beach!

Hi Pablo,

Thanks for your email and the photos of the snow in the mountains near Madrid. It looks so cold! You won't believe it, but here in Perth it's really hot. In Australia, Christmas is in summer, because we are in the southern hemisphere. Yesterday it was 38 degrees!

On Christmas Day, we had a barbecue in the garden with my grandparents, my aunts and my cousins. We ate prawns, salads and a dessert called pavlova, which is made with meringue, cream and fruit. In the afternoon, we went to the beach and played cricket on the sand. Some people even wear Santa hats when they go surfing!

How do you celebrate Christmas in Spain? Is it true that you get presents from the Three Kings on 6th January? That sounds amazing. I'd love to try the roscón you told me about.

Write back soon and tell me everything!

Best wishes,
Mia 🦘

PS: Here's a photo of me and my dog Bluey on the beach.

1. The parts of an email

An email has several parts: the address (To:), the subject (asunto: what it is about), the greeting (saludo), the body (the message, in paragraphs), the closing (despedida) and your name.

En castellano: el asunto debe ser corto y claro, por ejemplo «Party on Saturday!» o «Photos from the trip». Así la otra persona sabe de qué trata antes de abrirlo. Después del saludo ponemos una coma y empezamos el texto en la línea de abajo.

2. Greetings and closings

In an informal email (to friends and family) we start with Hi…, Hello…, or Dear…, and we finish with Love, (family and close friends), See you soon, Bye for now, Take care, or Best wishes,.

In a formal email we start with Dear Mr Smith, / Dear Ms Jones, / Dear Sir or Madam, and finish with Kind regards, or Yours sincerely,. En castellano: es como la diferencia entre «¡Hola, Pablo!» y «Estimado señor:».

3. Short forms and emojis

In messages to friends, people often use short forms (abreviaturas) and emojis. Here are some common ones in English:

  • BTW = by the way (por cierto)
  • LOL = laughing out loud (me parto de risa)
  • ASAP = as soon as possible (lo antes posible)
  • BRB = be right back (ahora vuelvo)
  • IDK = I don't know (no sé)
  • TBH = to be honest (la verdad)
  • Thx = thanks · pls = please · u = you · gr8 = great · CU = see you

Emojis can show feelings and make a message friendlier: 😊 👍 🎉 ❤️ 😂. But be careful:

  • Use short forms and emojis only with friends and family, in informal messages.
  • Never use them in formal emails, for example to a teacher, a company or a museum.
  • Don't use too many: your message should still be easy to read.
  • Emojis can be misunderstood. A message that seems funny to you might seem rude to someone else.

In your English exams, always write the full words: you, not u; great, not gr8.

4. Useful phrases

Opening: «How are you?», «Thanks for your email», «It was great to hear from you», «Sorry I didn't write sooner». Giving news: «Guess what!», «I've got some exciting news», «Last weekend I…».

Asking: «What about you?», «Can you come?», «Write back soon!». Ending: «I hope to see you soon», «Say hello to your family», «That's all for now». Consejo: estas frases hechas son como piezas de Lego: con ellas tu correo sonará natural.

5. Paragraphs

Organise the body in paragraphs (párrafos), one idea in each. A good plan for a short email: 1) greeting and why you are writing; 2) your news or the main information; 3) questions for your friend; 4) closing.

Leave a blank line between paragraphs. Keep sentences short and clear. En castellano: un correo de una sola parrafada es difícil de leer; separar las ideas ayuda a quien lo recibe.

6. Messages for special occasions

Emails and cards are perfect for special moments. Here are some useful phrases:

  • Birthdays: «Happy birthday! Have a fantastic day!» «Many happy returns!» «I hope all your wishes come true.»
  • Congratulations (for winning, passing an exam, a new baby…): «Congratulations! Well done!» «I'm so proud of you!» «You deserve it!»
  • Get well soon (when someone is ill): «I'm sorry to hear you're ill.» «Get well soon!» «I hope you feel better soon.»
  • Saying sorry: «I'm really sorry about…» «I didn't mean to…» «It won't happen again.»
  • Good luck: «Good luck in your exam!» «Fingers crossed!» «You can do it!»
  • Holidays: «Merry Christmas and a Happy New Year!» «Happy holidays!» «Have a great summer!»

Notice: in English we say «Happy birthday» and «Merry Christmas», but «Happy New Year» and «Happy Easter».

A short, personal message is always better than a long, general one. Add something special: a memory, a joke or a plan for when you see each other.

7. Connectors

Connectors join ideas: and (y) adds information, but (pero) shows a contrast, because (porque) gives a reason, so (así que) gives a result, and also (también) adds an idea.

«I love my new school because the teachers are very nice». «It was raining, so we stayed at home». «The film was long but exciting». Order words: first, then, after that, finally. Consejo: usa al menos tres conectores distintos en cada email.

8. Reading: an email from a friend

Read the email. Subject: My birthday party! «Hi Lucas, How are you? Thanks for the photos of your holiday. They're fantastic! Guess what! It's my birthday next Saturday and I'm having a party at the climbing centre. It starts at five o'clock and finishes at eight. My mum is going to make a big chocolate cake. Can you come? Please tell me because I need to book the places. Write back soon! Love, Mia»

Answer: Where is the party? What time does it start? Why does Mia need an answer?

9. Writing a reply

A reply (respuesta) answers all the questions. Lucas writes: «Hi Mia, Thanks for the invitation! I'd love to come to your party. Climbing is my favourite sport. My dad can take me, so I'll be there at five. Do I need special shoes? See you on Saturday! Lucas».

If you can't go, say sorry and give a reason: «I'm really sorry, but I can't come because I'm visiting my grandparents». En castellano: responde siempre a la pregunta principal al principio, y luego añade detalles.

Vídeo: Cambridge KEY A2: email writing, easy guide · The Nicholas Ross Academy (YouTube) · 123 mil visualizaciones

10. Check before you send

Before clicking Send, use this checklist: Is the subject clear? Did I use a greeting and a closing? Are there paragraphs? Did I answer all the questions? Did I use capital letters for names, days and months (Monday, July) and for I? Are the verbs in the right tense?

Safety online: only write to people you know, never share passwords or your address with strangers, and ask an adult if a message seems strange. En castellano: en internet, la prudencia es lo primero.

11. Before email: letters and postcards

Before email and mobile phones, people communicated by letter. They wrote by hand, put the letter in an envelope, wrote the address and put a stamp on it. Then the post took days or even weeks to arrive!

  • The world's first postage stamp, the Penny Black, appeared in the United Kingdom in 1840. It had a picture of Queen Victoria.
  • Postcards became very popular in the 20th century. People sent them from holidays with a photo on the front and a short message on the back: «Having a great time! Wish you were here!»
  • The first email was sent in 1971 by an American engineer called Ray Tomlinson. He chose the symbol @ (at) to separate the name of the person from the name of the computer. We still use it today!

Today, email is instant and free, but a handwritten letter or postcard is still special. Many people keep letters from family and friends for their whole lives. Why don't you send a real postcard to someone you love? They will be really happy to find it in their letterbox.

Vídeo: Raymond Tomlinson - the inventor of email · technogeiser (YouTube) · 82 mil visualizaciones

12. Let's practise: email exchange

Write an email to a pen friend (amigo por correspondencia) from another country. Tell them about you, your family, your school and your town. Ask three questions. Swap emails with a partner and write a reply.

Use this model: «Hi Sam, My name is Pablo and I'm eleven. I live in Teruel, a small city in Spain. I've got one sister. I love football and drawing, but I don't like Maths very much! What about you? What sports do you play? Write back soon! Best wishes, Pablo».

13. Saying thank you

A thank-you email is short, but it makes people very happy. It's polite to send one after someone gives you a present, invites you to their house or helps you.

A good thank-you email has four parts:

  • Greeting: «Dear Aunt Lucy,» or «Hi Tom,»
  • Thank them for something specific: «Thank you so much for the book you gave me for my birthday.» Saying exactly what you are thanking them for is more personal than just «Thanks for the present».
  • Say why you like it or how you used it: «I've already read three chapters. It's really exciting, and I love the main character!»
  • Close warmly: «I hope to see you soon. Thanks again! Love, Ana» or «Best wishes, Ana».

Useful phrases: Thank you so much for…, It was really kind of you to…, I really appreciate…, It's exactly what I wanted!, I had a great time at…

For a teacher or an adult you don't know well, use a more formal style: «Dear Mrs Smith, Thank you very much for organising the trip. We all learned a lot. Kind regards, Class 6B.»

14. Pen pals

A pen pal (or pen friend) is a friend in another country that you write to regularly. Many schools have exchanges with schools in other countries, for example through the European programme eTwinning. It's a great way to practise English and learn about other cultures.

In your first message, introduce yourself:

  • Your name, age and where you live: «My name's Pablo. I'm eleven and I live in Toledo, a historic city in the centre of Spain.»
  • Your family and pets.
  • Your school and favourite subjects.
  • Your hobbies and likes.
  • Something special about your town or country: a festival, a typical dish, a famous place.

Then ask questions to start a conversation: «What's your school like? What do you do at weekends? What's the weather like in your town now? Do you have any pets?»

Remember the safety rules: write only through your school or with your parents' permission, never share your address, passwords or private photos, and tell an adult if anything makes you feel uncomfortable.

Vídeo: How to Write a Friendly Letter · USPS (YouTube) · 436 mil visualizaciones

Ejemplos resueltos

Ejemplo 1. Choose a greeting and a closing for an email to your cousin.

  1. Es informal: familia.
  2. Saludo: Hi… o Dear… Despedida: Love,

Resultado: Hi Marta, … Love, Jaime

Ejemplo 2. Join with a connector: «I was tired. I went to bed early.»

  1. La segunda frase es el resultado.
  2. Resultado → so.

Resultado: I was tired, so I went to bed early.

Ejemplo 3. Write a good subject for an email about a school trip to the zoo.

  1. Corto y claro.
  2. Dice de qué trata.

Resultado: Subject: Our trip to the zoo!

Ejemplo 4. Rewrite for a teacher: «Hi! IDK the homework 4 tmrw, pls tell me ASAP 😅»

  1. Formal greeting and full words.
  2. No short forms or emojis.

Resultado: Dear Mr Brown, I'm sorry, but I don't know what the homework for tomorrow is. Could you tell me, please? Thank you. Best regards, Pablo.

Ejemplo 5. Make it more specific: «Thanks for the present.»

  1. Say exactly what the present was.
  2. Add why you like it.

Resultado: Thank you so much for the football. I played with it all weekend!

Errores típicos

  • Olvidar el asunto o poner uno vago como «Hello».
  • Escribir todo en un solo párrafo sin separar ideas.
  • Usar formal e informal a la vez: «Hi Mr Smith… Love,».
  • No usar mayúsculas en I, nombres, días y meses: «i», «monday».
  • No responder a todas las preguntas del email recibido.
  • Usar abreviaturas o emojis en un correo formal o en un examen.
  • Dar las gracias de forma general («Thanks for the present») en lugar de decir qué te gustó.

Ejercicios (24)

Hazlos en tu cuaderno y después abre la solución.

Nivel básico

  1. Name four parts of an email.

    Ver solución
    Subject, greeting, body, closing (y To / name).

  2. Write two informal closings.

    Ver solución
    Love, / Best wishes, / See you soon, / Bye for now,

  3. Is «Kind regards» formal or informal?

    Ver solución
    Formal.

  4. What does BTW mean?

    Ver solución
    By the way.

  5. Complete: «Get ___ soon!»

    Ver solución
    well.

  6. When was the first email sent?

    Ver solución
    In 1971.

  7. What season is Christmas in Australia?

    Ver solución
    Summer.

  8. What is a pen pal?

    Ver solución
    A friend in another country that you write to.

Nivel medio

  1. Complete: «I'm happy ___ it's Friday!»

    Ver solución
    because.

  2. Complete: «I like pizza, ___ I don't like olives.»

    Ver solución
    but.

  3. Correct the capitals: «on monday i'm going to london.»

    Ver solución
    On Monday I'm going to London.

  4. Write an opening sentence to thank a friend for their email.

    Ver solución
    Thanks for your email! / It was great to hear from you.

  5. Write a sentence to say no to an invitation politely.

    Ver solución
    I'm really sorry, but I can't come because I've got a match.

  6. Write a message to a friend who has broken her leg.

    Ver solución
    Open answer. Example: I'm so sorry to hear about your leg. Get well soon!

  7. Write the full words: thx, pls, u, gr8.

    Ver solución
    thanks, please, you, great.

  8. Why did Ray Tomlinson use @?

    Ver solución
    To separate the person's name from the computer's name.

  9. Write a short thank-you email to your grandma for a present.

    Ver solución
    Open answer.

  10. Answer Mia's question: How do you celebrate Christmas in Spain?

    Ver solución
    Open answer. Example: We have a big dinner on 24th December and the Three Kings bring presents on 6th January.

Nivel avanzado

  1. What should you never share in an email to a stranger?

    Ver solución
    Passwords, your address, phone number or photos.

  2. Write a short email (40 words) to invite a friend to the cinema.

    Ver solución
    Model answer: Hi Leo, Do you want to come to the cinema on Saturday? There's a new animated film. It starts at six. My mum can pick you up. Write back soon! Bye, Nora

  3. Write a congratulations email to a friend who won a competition (60 words).

    Ver solución
    Open answer.

  4. Write your first email to a pen pal (80 words) with three questions.

    Ver solución
    Open answer.

  5. Write a postcard from a holiday: where you are, what you're doing, the weather.

    Ver solución
    Open answer.

  6. Explain when emojis are a good idea and when they are not.

    Ver solución
    Good with friends in informal messages; not in formal emails or exams.

¿Has nombrado estas ideas?
★

Situación de aprendizajePen pals project

La clase inicia un intercambio de correos en inglés con un colegio de otro país.

Pasos

  1. Con ayuda del profesorado, buscad un colegio socio (por ejemplo, a través de eTwinning).
  2. Escribid un primer correo de presentación con preguntas.
  3. Responded a los correos recibidos y enviad mensajes para fechas especiales.
  4. Al final del trimestre, escribid un correo de agradecimiento y una postal real.

Producto final: Un intercambio de correos y postales con alumnos de otro país.

Cómo se valora

  • Uses the right style (formal or informal).
  • Writes messages for special occasions.
  • Asks and answers questions.
  • Follows online safety rules.

Tarjetas de repasoToca la tarjeta para darle la vuelta

Según cómo respondas, la tarjeta vuelve mañana, en 3, en 7 o en 21 días.

Para familias

  • Escribid juntos un email corto en inglés a un familiar o amigo y revisadlo con la lista del bloque 8.
  • Hablad sobre seguridad en internet: qué datos no se comparten nunca.
  • Repasad juntos las tarjetas del paso 6 dos minutos al día durante una semana.

Para profesores

Saberes: Comprensión y producción de textos escritos breves: el correo electrónico informal; conectores; normas de cortesía y seguridad digital (Lengua Extranjera) (RD 157/2022, tercer ciclo de Primaria).

  • Intercambio de emails con un colegio de otro país (eTwinning).
  • Correo de invitación y respuesta por parejas.
  • Corrección entre iguales con la lista de comprobación.

Qué vas a aprender

  • Recognise the parts of an email (partes de un correo)
  • Read an email and find key information
  • Write an informal email to a friend with greetings, paragraphs and closings
  • Use connectors and check your writing
  • Know when to use short forms and emojis
  • Write messages for special occasions
  • Learn about letters and postcards before email
  • Write thank-you emails and messages to a pen pal

Palabras clave

email · To / Subject · greeting · Dear… / Hi… · paragraph · closing · Best wishes · connectors: and, but, because, so · reply

Tiempo

80 minutos hoy + 2 minutos en cada repaso
